12514.text: The looking-ahead words are used most often against another person. It is placed in the heart: "let none of you devise evil against another in your heart" (Zec 7:10), "do not devise evil in your hearts against one another" (Zec 8:17). It is done together: "Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah" (Jer 18:18); "In Heshbon they planned disaster against her" (Jer 48:2); "they made plans to put him to death" (Joh 11:53), and Lazarus as well (Joh 12:10); "The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners" (Act 27:42). It is aimed at the righteous and the weak: "The wicked plots against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him" (Psa 37:12); "who have planned to trip up my feet" (Psa 140:4). It hides behind a friendly word: "Come and let us meet together" "But they intended to do me harm" (Neh 6:2); Saul's bride-price, "Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines" (1Sa 18:25). It is pinned on the other side: "you and the Jews intend to rebel" (Neh 6:6). Another pleads against it: Esther "pleaded with him to avert the evil plan of Haman" (Est 8:3; 9:24).

12519.text: God's plan takes in what people do against him without excusing them: "this Jesus, delivered up according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God, you crucified and killed by the hands of lawless men" (Act 2:23); "to do whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place" (Act 4:28).

15701.text: H2342J and H2342K (chul, 9 verses combined, glossed to twist: dance and to twist: anticipate) have no bearing on moral perversion: every verse is literal, a woman dancing (2 Sam 3:29's negated wish), waiting anxiously (Ps 37:7, Mic 1:12, Judg 3:25), a dove sent out and waited for (Gen 8:10). The root's full range (dance, whirl, writhe in labor, wait) has nothing to do with corruption; it was pulled into this family only because one of its senses translates as twist. 15803.text: H2342J and H2342K (both chul, split by sense) have real, coherent meaning covering dancing, whirling, waiting anxiously and writhing in childbirth. Their combined 10 occurrences are literal in every case: a whirling storm-tempest (Jer 23:19, 30:23), a spindle or dance reference in a curse formula (2 Sam 3:29), the voice of the Lord making a deer give birth (Ps 29:9), a sword raging against cities (Hos 11:6), and anxious waiting (Ps 37:7, Gen 8:10, Judg 3:25, Mic 1:12). None describes moral perversion.

15804.text: H2342K's occurrences (the same root's wait or anticipate sense) are likewise all literal waiting, none moral: Ps 37:7's counsel to wait patiently, Gen 8:10's dove sent out and waited for, Judg 3:25's servants waiting outside a chamber, Mic 1:12's anxious waiting for good news.

19653.text: Isaiah 1:29 — "the oaks that you desired … the gardens that you have chosen": The oracle opens as a lawsuit: *"Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth"* (v2). The charge goes to the inner being: *"Children have I reared and brought up, but they have rebelled against me"* (v2); *"The ox knows its owner … but Israel does not know, my people do not understand"* (v3); *"The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint"* (v5); Their worship goes on, and the Lord refuses it: *"I do not delight in the blood of bulls"* (v11); *"your appointed feasts my soul hates"* (v14); *"even though you make many prayers, I will not listen"* (v15).; Then the choice is laid before them, in the same two-sided shape as Isa 7:15: *"cease to do evil, learn to do good"* (v16–17); *"Come now, let us reason together"*, with the offer that sins *"like scarlet"* shall be *"as white as snow"* (v18); the two outcomes: *"If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land"*; *"but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be eaten by the sword"* (v19–20); Being willing, and refusing (here H3985, a different word from Isa 7), are the two sides of the choice. Eating, and being eaten, are its two outcomes.; The oracle ends with those who did not take the offer. v29–31 is figurative speech, and the figure is the point: *"they shall be ashamed of the oaks that you desired; and you shall blush for the gardens that you have chosen"*; *"you shall be like an oak whose leaf withers, and like a garden without water"*; *"the strong shall become tinder, and his work a spark, and both of them shall burn together"*; The things they desired and chose become the picture of what they themselves become. They chose oaks and gardens, and they become a withering oak and a garden with no water. The choice comes back as an image of the chooser. The last line goes further: the strong man’s own *"work"* is the spark that sets him alight. What he made burns him, *"with none to quench them"*.; Shame comes first in the verse: *"ashamed"*, *"blush"* (H0954, H2659). The chooser is ashamed of the very thing that was desired and chosen. What drew the desire becomes the cause of the shame.

It places the increase next to the choosing; it does not say one caused the other.

20490.text: 9.3 From thought to action (Claude's reading): The verses trace a path from thought to deed: Arising. Thoughts come, often in the night (Dan 2:29; Job 4:13; Ezek 38:10; Luke 24:38).; Lodging. They stay and are dwelt on (Jer 4:14).; Reckoning. They weigh up and value things (Isa 53:4; 1 Sam 1:13).; Devising. They take the form of a plan (Ezek 38:10b; Ps 36:4).; Expression. Tongue, lips and eyes: "your tongue plots" (Ps 52:2), "devise words of deceit" (Ps 35:20), "winks his eyes plans" (Prov 16:30), "whisper … imagine the worst" (Ps 41:7).; Action. Hand and feet: "when the morning dawns, they perform it" (Mic 2:1); "a heart that devises … feet that make haste" (Prov 6:18); "their feet run to evil … their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity" (Isa 59:7).; The same path also runs toward good: "When I think on my ways, I turn my feet to your testimonies" (Ps 119:59).

20491.text: Where responsibility sits. The commands address the stages from lodging onward: "forsake … his thoughts" (Isa 55:7); "let none of you devise evil" (Zech 7:10); "take every thought captive" (2 Cor 10:5); "wash your heart" (Jer 4:14); The *arising* is not commanded, but it is not neutral either. What comes up shows the condition of the heart (Gen 6:5; Mark 7:21). So thoughts that arise reveal the heart, and devising engages the will. The heart itself can be changed from outside: written on, given discretion, guarded, or darkened.

20909.text: What is downcast is their faces, the outward show of their state.

20910.text: Joseph asks; Pharaoh's officers in custody are the ones asked.

20911.text: The officers' faces are downcast; Joseph is the one who sees it and asks.

20912.text: Joseph has seen that they were troubled (Gen 40:6) and they are confined in his master's house.

20913.text: Joseph asked the officers the reason for their downcast faces.

20914.text: The officers' faces show sorrow today.

20915.text: Joseph asks why their faces are downcast, and they answer that they have dreamed and no one interprets (Gen 40:8).

20916.text: The downcast faces prompt his question: the question names the faces as what he asks about.

20917.text: Discovery: what lies behind the downcast faces is not stated in this verse; the passage gives their answer (Gen 40:8).

21282.text: Quiet gives a peaceable nature: a calm and gentle disposition of a spirit, a life, a house, or a people, named by another word.

21311.text: Called here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21477.text: Righteousness is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

21504.text: Wicked gives a moral condition to what it binds (an upright heart, a righteous or wicked way, godly grief, walking uprightly, a sinful nation): the uprightness, godliness or wickedness of the heart, speech, way or conduct.

21508.text: Wickedness is here the wickedness, ungodliness or sinfulness of a person as a state or practice of the heart, set against godliness and what is right (ungodliness, a heart busy with iniquity, a wicked deed, sinful passions).
